subject: MSA Addendum: On-Prem Rights, Audit Window & Witnessing Plan
messages:
From: Sara Morales <contracts@novushealth.org>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 02 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial: MSA addendum request for on-prem deployment

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the product demo last week — Novus Health is keen to move forward with a private deployment for our imaging pipeline. Our legal and procurement teams reviewed the MSA and we have a handful of addendum asks specific to on-prem/VPC deployments. High level:

- License scope: we need explicit language that the customer may run a single production instance in a dedicated VPC and make copies for DR in the same territory.
- Audit access: we require a quarterly audit window (2 business days) with read-only remote access and the ability to witness snapshot creation.
- Escrow-like contingency: in the event of insolvency or material breach, we need a pathway to receive runtime snapshots and a recovery plan (preferably via an audited third-party custodian).
- SLAs & evidence: order form must include evidence items for operator competency and snapshot verification tests.

I've attached a draft Novus addendum (PDF + redline summary). Can your team confirm whether Redwood can (1) accept a limited audit window, (2) make a commitment around snapshot transfer mechanics, and (3) provide the evidence checklist? Also please propose times for a legal sync next week.

Appreciate a short call to resolve the mechanics.

Best,
Sara Morales
Contracts Manager, Novus Health
contracts@novushealth.org
Attachment: Novus_MSA_Addendum_Draft.docx (docx)
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Sara Morales <contracts@novushealth.org>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 02 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial: MSA addendum request for on-prem deployment

Sara — thanks, really helpful summary and the draft. Looping in our legal and ops leads.

Short answers up front:
- Audit window: we can support a scheduled quarterly audit window (2 business days), with options for remote observation and a short on-site witness if mutually agreed in advance. We will not provide persistent live operator credentials; access is read-only via time-limited session tokens and recorded session logs.
- Snapshot transfer: we can provide verified runtime snapshots and a transfer manifest. For customer peace-of-mind we typically offer a notarized delivery to a named custodian or a downloadable encrypted snapshot delivered through a signed transfer protocol. We need to negotiate the triggering conditions (insolvency vs. inability to remediate).
- Evidence checklist: attached is our evidence_playbook_v0.9.pdf — it lists operator capability tests, witness steps for snapshot creation, and the sample manifest.

Next steps I propose:
1) Legal sync (30m) between Redwood legal + Novus contracts to agree on triggering events, custody wording, and the audit mechanics.
2) Ops runbook walk-through to confirm the snapshot format and witness steps.

Lauren/Sean — please review Novus' draft and the attached playbook; highlight any non-starters and suggested redlines. Sara — are you available for a legal sync on Mon 8/16 10:00-10:30 PT or Tue 8/17 11:00-11:30 PT?

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
T: +1 415 555 0189
Attachment: evidence_playbook_v0.9.pdf (pdf)
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 06 Aug 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: proposed redlines & negotiation approach for Novus Health addendum

Team — I reviewed Novus' draft and flagged items in redlines_proposal.pdf (attached). Key recommended positions:

- Accept: scheduled quarterly audit windows (2 business days), remote witness and recorded sessions, and a published manifest for snapshots. These preserve transparency without granting continuous access.
- Push back: any language implying "customer custody" or transfer of perpetual operational control to the customer. We should offer a certified snapshot plus transfer manifest and an escrow-style handoff to a vetted custodian only under narrow insolvency-triggered conditions.
- Clarify: scope of "copies for DR" — we should limit to a single DR instance per territory and require the Order Form to enumerate locations.
- Evidence: agree to provide operator competency evidence (test runbook, checklist outcomes, retained session logs), but limit retention to contractual retention period and audit-specific exports.

Negotiation talking points for the call:
1) Define triggering events for custodian transfer (material breach, insolvency, prolonged inability to remediate >60 days).
2) Use encrypted snapshot transfer with an HSM-backed key escrow — Redwood will not escrow private keys to the customer.
3) Offer a vetted third-party custodian option; if Novus insists on a named custodian, require a mutual acceptance clause.

Marissa — please prepare a concise redline file focused on the custody trigger language and the evidence retention cap. If we can secure the above, we can accept Novus' audit cadence.

Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redlines_proposal.pdf (pdf)
From: Sara Morales <contracts@novushealth.org>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@novushealth.org
Date: Tue, 12 Aug 2026 14:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA Addendum: On-Prem Rights, Audit Window & Witnessing Plan

Thanks Tessa and Lauren — this is helpful and close to what Novus needs. A few clarifications from our side after internal review:

- Custody trigger: Novus' legal team will accept insolvency or a failure-to-remediate trigger, but they want a maximum remediation cure period of 45 days (vs proposed 60). Can Redwood accommodate 45 days?
- DR copies: acceptable to limit to 1 DR instance per territory; please add a clause that DR copies are for failover only and cannot be used to serve production traffic.
- Snapshot transfer mechanics: Novus prefers either (a) Redwood-delivered encrypted snapshot to a mutually agreed custodian, or (b) a staged handoff where Novus downloads an encrypted snapshot after witnessed verification. We are open to the HSM-backed key approach — please provide draft language.

Attached is a short redlines_summary_from_novus.pdf highlighting the three asks above. We are available for a 30-minute legal sync on Mon 8/16 at 10:00 PT to run through the custody trigger and the snapshot handoff language. If that works, please send calendar invite.

Appreciate the collaboration.
Sara Morales
Contracts Manager, Novus Health
Attachment: redlines_summary_from_novus.pdf (pdf)
